items.body: A moment in adulthood arrives, sooner or later, when your childhood neighborhood starts looking like a movie set built from memory: the curb seems smaller, the houses fake, the corner store guilty. NYIKO’s Neighborhood lives in that unnerving dislocation, where leaving home turns out to be less dramatic than realizing another place has become home while life made other plans. The song has the good sense to keep its hands off the panic button, though. Guitars jangle with a tone that brings Echo and the Bunnymen to mind, while NYIKO sings with a wounded restraint that brushes against The Smiths and Choir Boy. The arrangement gives the melody room to wander, lets the bass and drums hold their ground, and trusts the ache in the vocal to do more work than production could. NYIKO has moved through hip hop, piano songwriting, emo, hardcore, and electronic music, and you can hear the benefit of that restlessness in the way Neighborhood sidesteps purity tests. The song feels pop-minded without becoming smug about hooks, emotionally direct without begging for sympathy. Somewhere in its DNA sits the plainspoken intelligence of Magnetic Fields and Divine Comedy, that knack for taking a condition and phrasing it as though you overheard the right sentence at the wrong time. Directed and edited by Sabrina Gimenez, the video for Neighborhood follows people moving separately through a residential area before their bodies begin slipping into rhythmic glitches. A twitch here, a repeated gesture there, then these isolated figures start syncing up, as if the neighborhood itself has found a tempo and decided everybody ought to obey it. At golden hour, they converge in a brief group movement before the pattern breaks apart. Everybody disperses, except one person who keeps going. NYIKO, who produced and choreographed the video, turns belonging into something halfway between comfort and contagion. Community looks beautiful for a second, then faintly sinister once you notice how easily individual behavior can fall into step. Watch Neighborhood below: That idea runs straight into Fate, NYIKO’s sophomore album, released September 16 through Trailing Twelve Records. Across ten songs, he considers desire, identity, attachment, politics, memory, and the unseen systems nudging people toward choices they swear are entirely their own. “I wanted to write an album about the invisible forces that shape our lives,” says NYIKO. “Whether it’s the internet, politics, nostalgia, celebrity culture, or our own attachment patterns, we spend so much time believing we’re making independent choices without realizing how much we’re being pulled by things outside ourselves. Every song asks the same question from a different angle: how much of our lives is fate, and how much is choice?” Opening track O Primate sets chiming synthesizers against jangling guitars, its wavering electronic tones giving the brighter riffs an agreeable instability. Warm bass anchors NYIKO’s phrasing, which has something of The Smiths’ conversational elasticity: a melody that seems to discover its own argument as the sentence unfolds. Beneath that inviting surface sits a consideration of animal rights, human power, and the ease with which cruelty becomes ordinary. When clipped, piano-like keyboard notes enter midway through, they sharpen the arrangement without disturbing its composure. His measured delivery gives the subject room, keeping the listener close enough to sit with an uncomfortable question. On Stay Young, hazy synthesizers and a gentle bass figure make way for a new wave vocal over unhurried drums. Its wish to suspend youth carries the knowledge that adulthood keeps changing the people and places we count on. As the bass grows fuller, guitars broaden into the generous shapes of 1980s pop-rock, with vocal harmonies adding lift. There is an appealing ease to the way these parts gather around the melody, each arrival making the song feel a little more expansive. For a few minutes, NYIKO makes holding on sound effortless, even as the title betrays how much effort might be involved. The piano-led opening of camgirl brings Corey Hart’s earnest new wave balladry to mind, with soft vocals and small harmony accents lending the first stretch an almost private scale. Inspired by the psychological thriller Cam, the song follows a lonely fan who mistakes a sex worker’s paid attention for a romance. NYIKO lets us hear the tenderness that makes the misunderstanding persuasive to the person having it. Midway through, a funkier bass line, firmer drums, and more expressive guitars enlarge the arrangement, carrying his fantasy toward the proportions of a grand declaration. The musical uplift makes his certainty feel alarmingly easy to share. Sugar brings a cooler, more physical tension, somewhere between Mareux’s controlled darkwave and Provoker’s bruised intimacy. Angular guitars interrupt the synth swells, while a substantial bass line gives the track weight and a certain weary grace. The album’s notes place it within the complexities of loving someone who works in the sex industry; desire, emotional distance, and control all bear on the relationship. NYIKO’s delivery catches that difficult balance between wanting another person and recognising how much of yourself you are surrendering to the arrangement. The rhythm keeps moving with an assurance the relationship seems unable to sustain. “To me, Sugar is about temptation and control,” NYIKO confesses. “It’s what happens when lust overrides logic – when something looks sweet on the surface but rots you from the inside.” Rippling synths introduce SUPERFAN, where a wistful vocal gradually acquires momentum from the drums and bass. Its apparent love song exposes the possessiveness that can turn celebrity admiration into entitlement. Chiming synthesizers and changes in pace give the arrangement a restless shape, repeatedly raising its emotional temperature before allowing it to settle. Those returns to relative calm are especially effective: NYIKO gives the melody enough breathing room for its sweetness to register. At each subsequent swell, the voice seems ready to make an enormous promise, leaving us to wonder who has actually agreed to receive it. An extended guitar melody holds Shelter steady while warm bass and drums establish a more welcoming momentum. Here, the search for home settles on the emotional security another person can offer. NYIKO’s pop-rock delivery has room to open up, and the bright, bubbling synthesizer that introduces the chorus supplies a welcome burst of pleasure. The beat becomes easier to dance to as the song expands, giving its optimism a physical expression. After the fraught attachments of the preceding tracks, that sustained guitar line sounds particularly reassuring, carrying the tune through its changes with an unforced sense of continuity. After Neighborhood, the title track Fate draws the album into darker territory. A compressed synthpop beat gradually comes into focus, revealing a wiry rhythm beneath NYIKO’s smooth delivery. Layered vocal harmonies lend the melody a slightly baroque elegance. The song explores an avoidant relationship, with desire repeatedly renewed by a lover’s retreat. Metallic keyboard tones and sighing synth pads enter around the midpoint, followed later by rippling melodic figures that make the arrangement feel increasingly unsettled. There is something rueful about how gracefully the vocals move through all this activity, as though the pleasure of singing could briefly make the uncertainty bearable. Drifting synthesizers give Victim of No Consequence an airy entrance before a buoyant bass line and gently floating drumbeat take over. NYIKO returns to a Smiths-like cadence, surrounded by jangling acoustic guitar and bright electronic accents. It is among the album’s most immediately memorable songs, with a tune that almost supplies its own invitation to sing along. The lyrics follow two young men drawn toward incompatible realities through pandemic misinformation and conspiracy culture. That inviting arrangement becomes an especially pointed setting: a melody capable of bringing voices together accompanies a song about people losing the ability to agree on what is real. Closing track Summer of Outrage opens out around warm bass, acoustic strumming, and a sustained guitar figure whose long, expressive reach recalls The Chameleons. The riff returns between verses, giving the song a recognizable center as NYIKO’s broad radio-pop vocal and bright synthesizers fill the space around it. Written in August 2020, the song holds the urgency of the Black Lives Matter protests alongside the isolation of lockdown and the exhausting churn of social media. Its public concerns eventually give way to a more personal grief over time apart from friends. A late passage of piano and voice brings that feeling into focus before the closing guitar expansion. The generosity of the melody makes a fitting conclusion to Fate: even after ten songs spent examining what draws people together and pulls them apart, NYIKO can still make connection sound possible. Listen to Fate below, and stream the album here. Follow NYIKO: Instagram TikTok YouTube Facebook Bandcamp The post LA New Wave Artist NYIKO Searches for Meaning and Connection in the Modern World on Second LP “Fate” — Watch Video for “Neighborhood” appeared first on Post-Punk.com.

items.body: Label: P&M Records, 2026 Personnel - Michael Blake: tenor and soprano saxophone; Gary Versace: piano; Ben Allison: bass; Michael Sarin: drums. Canadian-born, New York-based saxophonist and composer Michael Blake gathers a quartet of longtime collaborators for a slightly unsettling jazz session centered on Halloween, a holiday of imagination and transformation built around costumes, community, and the unexpected. Joining Blake here are pianist Gary Versace, bassist Ben Allison, and drummer Michael Sarin—all of whom have played and recorded with the saxophonist in various musical contexts. All nine compositions on the album are covers associated with Halloween, with the exception of the last track, Blake's " The Creep ", a shape-shifter showing many faces in minor mode with a bluesy feel. The opener, " Halloween ", slides in with mystery-induced suspense, leading to an atmospheric crescendo dreamily texturized by jagged piano chords in the high register. It keeps us engaged and alert as it moves forward in a fluid 5/4 time signature, strengthened by Blake's command of phrase and tone—he offers a haunting improvisation delivered with pure instinct and multiphonic impact. " Stalking Monster " and " Anatomy of a Murder " are Duke Ellington compositions, the former from Night Creature and the latter from Otto Preminger's film of the same name. " Stalking Monster " features tonally contrasting piano playing over hi-hat pulsation, creating eerie undertones before morphing into a 4/4 swing in the best that jazz tradition has to offer. An empowering feeling comes from the soloists: Blake is soulfully articulate while Versace introduces rich motivic ideas. This continuous fluidity, without straining to make a point, carries over to " Anatomy of a Murder ", a blues where bass and piano start in tandem, filling the lower register with gorgeous groove. The gears shift considerably on " The Great Pumpkin Waltz "—Vince Guaraldi's tune from the 1966 Halloween television special It's The Great Pumpkin, Charlie Brown —here delivered with harmonic sophistication and passionate lyricism. On soprano saxophone, Blake exudes clarity of technique and natural phrasing, switching to tenor on the following tune, " Transylvanian Lullaby ", the main haunting theme from Mel Brooks's 1974 comedy Young Frankenstein . Allison and Sarin build tension at the outset, and the piece becomes gently brushed after brief, well-devised staccato moves. The rhythm section compellingly swings in support of Blake's nimble solo. There's also a slow, rubato rendition of " Witchcraft ", Cy Coleman's tune popularized by Frank Sinatra and the Bill Evans Trio, where brooding melodicism comes to the fore. The chemistry between Blake and his rhythm team is undeniable throughout, even when the energy dips a bit after the first couple of tracks. Favorite Tracks: 01 - Halloween ► 02 - Stalking Monster ► 04 - Transylvanian Lullaby
items._cn_summary: 萨克斯演奏家 Michael Blake 携手长期合作的钢琴手 Gary Versace、贝斯手 Ben Allison 和鼓手 Michael Sarin，围绕万圣节主题呈现一张以翻唱曲目为主的四重奏专辑。除最后一首 Blake 原创的《The Creep》外，其余九首作品均与万圣节相关，包括 Duke Ellington 的《Stalking Monster》与《Anatomy of a Murder》、Vince Guaraldi 的《The Great Pumpkin Waltz》、Mel Brooks 电影《Young Frankenstein》中的《Transylvanian Lullaby》，以及 Frank Sinatra 曾演绎的《Witchcraft》。演奏风格扎根于主流爵士传统，包含 5/4 拍的神秘氛围、慢板自由节拍的布鲁斯改编以及带有暗黑抒情意味的演绎。评论提及 Blake 在高音区展现的清晰技术与多重音色运用，乐队化学反应在前几首之后略有下降。整体属于在既定爵士框架内进行主题化概念性编排的专辑，创新性有限。

Recorded on July 18, 1980, the album captures live versions of seven solo songs by Vega. items.body: Review by BrufordFreak — Over its near-20 years of existence, Utah's Rylee McDonald has seen his high school musical project turn into a kind of family affair, now adding his partner and wife and their two children to the mix. Still, the Rush- and Led Zeppelin-inspired artist has emerged as his own musical force.1. "In A Lone and Dreary World" (19:03) a djenty low end does not deter this prog extravaganza from taking us on a journey that reminds me of the music of 21st Century projects like LIFESIGNS and NUMEN and even COSMOGRAF and DAVE BRONS . . . (if a little metal edge were applied). Though I am not a fan of this kind of "plastic" drum sound, I very much appreciate the skills and creativity of the performance on the batterie exhibited here by Mike Lofgreen (though it is also mixed into the soundscape as a kind of anomaly of isolated individually-distinguished sterility; that is, the rest of the sounds are given those standard effects we now associate automatically with prog, i.e. reverbs, distortions, gates, sustains, compressions, etc.) Oh! really love the voice of Kristen McDonald. The collective sound of the band's vocal palette reminds me of short-lived band from Naughties, THE REASONING as well as second- and third- album PURE REASON REVOLUTION (2009's Amor Vincit Omnia and 2010's Hammer and Anvil). Paired up with those syncopated djenty guitar chords and we have quite a cool sound and mix. Then you have to take into consideration the common human plight being expressed in the song lyrics: dissatisfaction and distrust of all we've been raised to believe and value, all we've been told--including that coming from parents and family--learning to listen to and trust one's own inner voice and inner truths and beliefs--the awakening to the power of a spiritual perspective (perhaps even a Christian rebirth): "No enemies" and "saved and sound." Though the length taken to deliver the message/story is a bit over-protracted, it is effective and well-rendered with little or no fluff and appropriate nuance and theatrics. Nice work. (36.5/40) 2. "Faiths Window" (5:20) with industrial horn humming in the background a dirty-distorted electric guitar's two-chord strum repeats itself, occasionally moving between subtly different chords as Rylee McDonald sing/talks over the top, turning into singing as the rest of the band's sound cascades into the mix. It's heavy but it's symphonic with the layers of instruments easy to distinguish from each other. In the fourth minute the lyrics are delivered through growl-screams before the McDonald family choir takes over. A metal instrumental passage takes over with searing electric guitar, etc. but then Kristen emerges as the lead vocalist, taking us to the song's (rather sudden) end. (8.875/10)3. "Patience" (4:53) a normal rock sound palette over which Rylee's single male voice leads the way gradually turns heavy metal with the chorus, playing out as such into the final fadeout of electronic keyboards. A solid song but there is nothing very new or innovative here. (8.75/10)4. "Past Life Parable" (5:03) more solid heavy prog steering toward the more sophisticated hair band sounds and music of the 1970s and 1980s, the big difference here is the use of djenty guitar chords and some more-modern sounds as well as an admirable level of sophistication in the construct/composition. (8.875/10)5. "Gravity I" (2:35) nice Spanish acoustic guitar play surrounded by proggy drum 'n' bass and textural synth washes and other keyboard and, eventually, electric guitar effects. Impressive drum play toward the end--just before the transition/bridge to "Gravity II." (4.625/5) 6. "Gravity II" (4:49) bleeding over from the previous "introductory" song, Rylee's voice in the lead position is backed/doubled by Kristen. Nice use of organ bass pedals and harpsichord sound in the third minute, but then we are quickly back into the metal, even djenty music long before the minute's end. I really like the guitar djent-play in this section (as well as the more subdued vocal performance), but then we shift back into hyperdrive with the machine gun bass pedal play for a few bars before cutting out for a near-a cappella passage, but then we nearly as quickly and suddenly find ourselves back in the fray of machine gun beats and rapid-fire beat-down low end guitar chords. Still, I like and respect it overall. (9/10)7. "Animals" (5:34) Rylee's single male voice is singing while only accompanied by lone acoustic guitar picking. After one time through a round of the verse and chorus the keys, bass pedals, and stark drum play join in the now split (R & L) two-acoustic guitar picking foundation. I wish I could pick out who Rylee's voice reminds me of: it's definitely one of STYX's lead vocalists: either Tommy Shaw or Dennis DeYoung. The McDonald family choir is cited for this song but their role is, sadly, rather quiet, minor. Still, this is a pretty cool song--one that only lacks for seriously brainworm melodies. (9.125/10) Total Time 47:17The McDonald family's sound and style cannot help but be compared to the bands mentioned above--especially THE REASONING and early PURE REASON REVOLUTION but also bands like RUSH, STYX, INTROITUS and MEER. From its Led Zeppelin inspiration and Rush fueling and modeling, the band seems to have come into its own: into something that sounds like . . . but is really their own thing--which is really nice.A-/five stars; though this kind of Classic Rock and sophisticated 80s Metal blend of prog is not really among my high preferences, I do appreciate the creative and complex song structures built here as well as the wonderful vocal work rendered by the collective members of the McDonald family (really, Rylee and Kristen).
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由犹他州音乐人Rylee McDonald的家庭成员共同演绎，将高中时期的项目发展为家族合作。首曲近二十分钟的史诗式编制以Djent低音为底色，融合新世纪前卫乐队LIFESIGNS与NUMEN般的复杂编曲层次，歌词探讨对既有信仰体系的怀疑与个人精神觉醒。主唱Kristen McDonald的声线被比作THE REASONING与PURE REASON REVOLUTION，合唱段落为沉重器乐增添温度。短曲中工业嗡鸣与失真吉他交织，金属嘶吼与人声合唱交替登场。整体制作注重音色分层与空间感，鼓声混音较为孤立。作为前卫金属领域内技术扎实但风格偏向主流重金属谱系的家庭式创作，其编排与演奏具有一定复杂度，但在声音探索和跨界融合层面并未触及实验或电子领域。

items.body: Review by BrufordFreak — One of Radiohead's founding guitarists (and still member) Ed O'Brien releases his second studio album as a solo artist. I don't know any of the guest musician/collaborators but you can bet that Ed had his pick of the cr'me de la cr'me!1. "Incantations" (7:41) a single repeating acoustic guitar arpeggio provides the bed for 1:45 of Ed's folk singing. It honestly sounds like something from an early Roy Harper album. Other instruments, hand percussives and electronics, join in to move the music into territory previously traveled by the likes of DONOVAN and BJ'RK. Floating background vocals sound like Bj'rk's Inuit Choir on the Vespero tours. At 5:40 the percussionist(s) are joined by drums, electric bass, electric guitars, and keyboard atmospherics--which play out until slowly being faded out while Dave Okumu's bass and Ed's reverberating guitar notes continue to the song's end. Cool song! (13.875/15)2. "Blue Morpho" (6:18) another really cool atmospheric sonosphere created by guitars, wordless vocals, bass, synth washes, and, this time, full symphony strings. It's quite lovely--even moving: chords and multiple melody lines floating, flowing, shifting, morphing, and melding into one gorgeous textural feast. And the whole time I'm feel quite a little debt owed (or homage given) to George Martin and The Beatles. (Think of songs like "Blackbird" and "I Am the Walrus" as well as albums like Magical Mystery Tour.) Brilliant and beautiful! (9.75/10)3. "Sweet Spot" (4:10) double lines of picked acoustic guitar chords woven into one though coming from both sides of the stage starts out this beautiful, atmospheric and kind of eerie (like GRAVENHURST) music over/within which Ed sings both lead and backing vocals. I like the way the orchestra strings slowly move to the fore as Ed's lead voice sinks into the instrumental mix. Eventually, the strings (and, I'll assume, keyboard electronics) end up alone, finishing the song after everybody/everything else has left. Not as memorable as the previous songs but rewarded for the creative sound and structural tactics. (9/10)4. "Teachers" (5:18) a funky bass 'n' drum pattern is surrounded and permeated by eerie atmospherics. Ed's heavily-treated ghost-voice enters toward the end of the first minute, singing in a pleasant monotone for a minute or so but then it leaves, whereupon the bass, drums, guitars, and synths all seem to spread out into loose, adventurous swaths away from but still anchored in the main theme. The final minute sees the vocal choir sing, "open wide" before the instruments all stop or fade away, leaving only weird electronic noises to close out the song. (8.875/10)5. "Solfeggio" (2:36) guitar/electronic harpsichord chord perpetuated with sustain and arpeggiation open this before more layers of voice-originating atmospherics enter and steer the with an eerie yet unthreatening kind of melody line, repeated over and over before signing off with a final lower-register three-note sequence, all the while the glitchy electronica effects are increasingly present, even rising to a driver's position, like something from a SyFy Continuum soundtrack experience (think Au4's "Everyone Is Everyone [and Everything Is Everything]"). More genius song/sound making. (4.4375/5)6. "Thin Places" (2:19) flute, wordless voice, synthetics all woven together to create a kind of dream-like out-of-body astral travel experience. (4.4375/5)7. "Obrigado" (9:53) a very cool, almost jazz-lite rhythm track over/within which Ed & Co. deliver some pretty awesome atmospherics (as well as vocals). The reverse-delay guitar effects for Ed's guitar solo in the seventh and eighth minutes are only surpassed by the dreamy psychedelic soundscape floating and morphing beneath it (and, later, by the amazing wordless vocal tracks raging in the background--which I think one must attribute to Clare Torey-inspired Awsa Berstrom). Ed's ultra-cool voice reminds me of both George Harrison, Gadi Caplan, Donovan, and Harry Nilsson as well as, you know, Radiohead. Really a cool, amazing, and powerful song. A pleasure to listen to every single time I do. (19.5/20)Total Time 38:15It's weird how much/how often I hear core/key Radiohead sounds in Ed's music here. This leads me to feel strongly how important and integral he was/is to the Radiohead sound--to their music.A/five stars; a brilliant display of creative/innovative sound and song crafting that stands out as a masterpiece of extrapolated future music (as if Ed's projecting himself into the 22nd Century or beyond--or even another dimension). A modern musical masterpiece. Highly recommended. One of the best albums I've heard from 2026.
items._cn_summary: Radiohead成员Ed O'Brien的第二张个人专辑延续了其乐队作品中已显露的氛围化倾向。整张专辑以原声吉他分解和弦为底色，叠加电子合成器铺陈、管弦乐弦乐层和大量人声氛围处理，从Donovan式的民谣出发，逐步向Björk式的实验声景扩展。多首作品采用单一动机循环叠加的写法，乐器和人声在混音中逐渐隐退或浮现，结构上具有渐进式的演变逻辑。部分曲目如《Blue Morpho》被评论者指出与Beatles的编曲手法有隐性关联。《Teachers》则展示了节奏部分驱动的实验走向。整体而言，这是一张制作精良、注重音色质感与空间营造的氛围流行/民谣作品，但在类型突破性和实验深度上并未走得太远，对于追求前卫实验或自由即兴的听众来说可能偏向温和。

items.body: Suzanne Perry, the vocalist of 1990s dream pop duo Love Spirals Downwards, released the three-track EP “There’ll Be No More Promises” on Projekt Records on September 18, 2026. The EP is available as a name-your-price digital release on Bandcamp and through streaming and download platforms, and is described on its release page as dream pop, ethereal and darkwave. Perry recorded the EP with multi-instrumentalist Cris Miller of the solo dream-pop project Silver Screen. The lead and title track, “There’ll Be No More Promises,” is new material; the second track is a re-recording of the Love Spirals Downwards song “Ladonna Dissima,” originally released on the duo’s 1994 debut album “Idylls”; the third is a cover of Danny Elfman’s “Sally’s Song” from “The Nightmare Before Christmas.” Perry describes her songwriting process as “instinctively formed as an escape. I find myself captivated within the experience of honest expressionistic music brought into being from a deep introspective place.” Miller, discussing his approach to the collaboration, says he “pay[s] special attention to detail and pursue[s] a holistic approach: envisioning the entire sound first, allowing free experimentation during the process, knowing the direction of the song will be uncovered.” There’ll Be No More Promises (ep) by Suzanne Perry Perry is scheduled to perform live at Brickbat Mansion in Portland, Oregon, on Saturday, October 24, 2026. About Suzanne Perry Suzanne Perry is the vocalist of Love Spirals Downwards, the dream pop duo she formed with guitarist and producer Ryan Lum in Orange County, California, in the early 1990s. The project released its debut album, “Idylls,” in 1994, followed by “Flux” (1995), “Ardor” (1996) and “Ever” (1999), largely on Projekt Records, building a reputation within the American dream pop and ethereal scenes alongside labels including Projekt Records. Love Spirals Downwards has been inactive as a group for extended periods since, with Perry periodically re-emerging with new recordings. “There’ll Be No More Promises,” released September 18, 2026, reunites Perry with Projekt Records and pairs her with Cris Miller of Silver Screen. Alongside the new title track, the EP revisits Love Spirals Downwards’ own catalogue with a redesigned version of “Ladonna Dissima” and adds a cover of “Sally’s Song,” continuing the ethereal, harmony-driven sound Perry first established three decades ago.
items._cn_summary: Suzanne Perry 是1990年代梦幻流行二人组 Love Spirals Downwards 的主唱，她在 Projekt Records 厂牌发行了三曲 EP《There'll Be No More Promises》。这张作品由梦幻流行独立音乐人 Cris Miller 担任多乐器演奏与制作，包含一首新曲、一首对乐队1994年首张专辑中《Ladonna Dissima》的重新录制版本，以及一首改编自 Danny Elfman 为《圣诞夜惊魂》创作的《Sally's Song》。Perry 将创作描述为一种本能的逃逸，源于内省的诚实表达；Miller 则强调对细节的关注与整体声音的构想。整体延续了她三十年前所确立的以和声为核心的飘渺风格，没有明显的实验转向或跨界融合，主要面向梦幻流行与暗潮场景的既有听众。

items.body: Fernando’s Eyes releases the single “Room On Fire” on 25 September via Aenaos Records, the project‘s first new material since last year’s album “Center Of Your World” and its accompanying “Bonus Tracks & Remixes”. A video accompanies the release on the same day. You can pre-save the single right now. Fernando’s Eyes is the solo project of Fernando Honorato, singer and co-founder of Stockholm post-punk band Principe Valiente. “Room On Fire” moves with more directness than the atmospheric material on “Center Of Your World”: Honorato produced the track himself, with co-production and mix by Hans Olsson, layering programmed drums against live toms he played personally. A saxophone part by Swedish jazz musician Lina Langendorf cuts through the arrangement without turning ornamental. Honorato describes “Room On Fire” as a song about leaving without looking back, a deliberate choice rather than a loss, with the production’s forward momentum matching that resolve. About Fernando’s Eyes Fernando Honorato is the lead vocalist and primary songwriter of Principe Valiente, the Swedish post-punk and darkwave band he founded in 2005. In 2025, he opened a more personal creative outlet through the solo project Fernando’s Eyes, starting with the single “A Million Times” and followed by the debut album “Center Of Your World”. “Room On Fire” is the project’s first new single since that album.
items._cn_summary: Fernando's Eyes 是斯德哥尔摩后朋克乐队 Principe Valiente 主唱 Fernando Honorato 的个人计划，新单曲《Room On Fire》由他本人制作，Hans Olsson 参与联合制作与混音。编曲上以编程鼓机与真人手击的汤姆鼓叠加，瑞典爵士音乐人 Lina Langendorf 的萨克斯线条穿透整体编排而不流于装饰。Honorato 将这首歌描述为关于不回头地离开——一种主动选择而非失去，制作的向前推进感呼应这一决心。相比此前专辑《Center Of Your World》的氛围化质感，这首作品更为直接。Aenaos Records 是小型独立厂牌。整体而言，这是一篇以新闻发布形式呈现的乐评，侧重信息告知而非深度评论，文本偏短。

1975年、神奈川県横須賀市生まれ。早稲田大学第一文学部卒業後、2000年よりベルリン在住。著書に『明子のピアノ』（岩波ブックレット）、監修を務めた『おとうさんのポス... 詳しく見る 音楽の友 編集部 月刊誌 1941年12月創刊。音楽之友社の看板雑誌「音楽の友」を毎月刊行しています。“音楽の深層を知り、音楽家の本音を聞く”がモットー。今月号のコンテンツはこちらバックナンバ... 詳しく見る 音楽シーズンと共に幕を開ける音楽祭、ベルリン・ムジークフェストが今年も始まった。前身のベルリン芸術週間を含めると今回が75回目という節目で、とりわけ意欲的なプログラムが組まれている。8月28日のオープニング公演が、ニコラス・コロン指揮フィンランド放送交響楽団による、リゲティのオペラ《ル・グラン・マカーブル》であることも、その表れといえるだろう。 20世紀後半を代表するオペラだが、ベルリンでは比較的上演の機会に恵まれている。2003年のコーミッシェ・オーパー（バリー・コスキー演出）、2017年のサイモン・ラトル指揮ベルリン・フィルハーモニー管弦楽団（ピーター・セラーズ演出）に続き、筆者にとっては3度目の実演となる。 「架空の国ブリューゲルランドの国歌が演奏されますのでご起立ください」とアナウンスされ、実際に聴衆が立ち上がってから鳴り響くのが、12個のクラクションによるけたたましい前奏曲。演奏会形式の上演かと思いきや、歌手は全員インパクトの強い衣裳を身につけ、舞台上演に比べて遜色がない。 客席に配したバンダや合唱、子役を使った秘密政治警察「ゲポポ」の登場など、フィルハーモニーの空間を存分に生かした舞台である。ヴィーナスと「ゲポポ」長官の二役を超絶技巧で歌うソプラノのサラ・アリスティドウを始め、歌手陣は総じてすばらしい。フィンランド放送響も、その精緻で美しい響きを生かした申し分のない演奏を聴かせてくれた。 一方、全体主義政治を生き抜いたリゲティが書いた、非人間性や腐敗をテーマにしたこのオペラが、かつてのような風刺性を持ちにくくなっている実情も感じた。現実の独裁政治や自然災害のほうが、はるかにグロテスクかつ巨大な範囲で私たちを襲い続けているということなのだろう。 ではこうした野心的なプロダクションが意味を失っているのかと言えば、そんなことは決してないはずだ。ロシアと国境を接したフィンランドとの共同制作により、このオペラがフィンランドで初演された数日後にベルリンで上演されたことには意義があった。こうした国際的な連携自体が、時に有効な政治批評性を持つこともありうる。 サバール指揮コンセール・デ・ナシオンのメンデルスゾーン～刺激的かつフレッシュな《イタリア》 サバール指揮のコンサートは、もはや一回一回に聴き逃せない重みがある © Fabian Schellhorn ムジークフェスト2日目（8月29日）には、ジョルディ・サバールが手兵のコンセール・デ・ナシオンと客演した。本コーナーで同じ顔ぶれによる今年3月のオール・モーツァルトのコンサートを紹介しているが、サバール指揮の公演はもはや一回一回が聴き逃せない重みを増している。今回のオール・メンデルスゾーンのプログラムも、フィルハーモニーはほぼ満席だった。 メンデルスゾーン「交響曲第3番《スコットランド》」と「第4番《イタリア》」、その間に「序曲《フィンガルの洞窟》」を挟む、一見何の変哲もないプログラムだが、泰斗サバールの手にかかると夢のような時間に変わる。 とくに面白かったのが《イタリア》で、一般的に知られる1833年版ではなく、作曲家がその後手を加えた1834年版がベルリン公演で用いられた。この版で聴くと、とくに第2楽章から第4楽章までの印象がガラリと変わるのだ。 バスのオスティナートで進行する第2楽章は深い祈りのようで、サバールが語るように「J.S.バッハのコラールのような」瞬間さえある（彼はこの楽章をアンコールでもう一度指揮した）。第4楽章のサルタレッロでは、1833年版にはないティンパニの強打が加わり、嵐のように始まる。中間部で弦楽器セクションが目まぐるしいテンポで奏でる音型のやり取りは、ピリオド楽器のコンセール・デ・ナシオンによっていっそう明晰に浮かび上がる。これほど刺激的かつフレッシュな《イタリア》体験は初めてだった。 前半の《スコットランド》では陰影の深さと共に、スコットランドの民族舞踊の生き生きとした表現が光った。ムジークフェストへのインタヴューで、サバールは「私はかつて17世紀の原典を用いて、スコットランド音楽の研究に4年間を費やした」と明かしているが、あらゆる時代と地域の音楽を吸収してきたサバール指揮の演奏には、人間の文化のなかで育まれてきた音楽の「養分」がぎっしり詰まっている。
items._cn_summary: 本文报道2026年柏林音乐节开幕演出及次日音乐会。开幕场为芬兰广播交响乐团在尼古拉斯·科隆指挥下呈现利盖蒂歌剧《列日大神》，以音乐会形式演出但配以视觉化服装与舞台调度，利用柏林爱乐大厅空间布置了乐队、合唱团与童声演员。独唱阵容整体表现出色，尤其饰演维纳斯与秘密警察长官双角的次女高音萨拉·阿里斯蒂多展现了极高声乐技巧。次日萨瓦尔指挥和谐之花古乐团演绎门德尔松《苏格兰交响曲》《芬戈尔山洞序曲》及较少上演的1834年版《意大利交响曲》。后者版本在配器与段落结构上与通行的1833年版本差异显著，萨瓦尔的诠释强调第二乐章的巴赫式圣咏深度与第四乐章萨尔塔雷洛舞曲中定音鼓的雷霆效果，古乐器编制赋予作品更清晰的纹理与历史质感。

items.body: The Wind is a peaceful retreat, a meditation on the natural world, and a call to act on the threat of climate change when inactivity and tepid response has become a disturbing norm. The Wind also details the ancient tale of a saint who carried the wind to an airless French valley, and in a similar way, Balmorhea’s debut release on Deutsche Grammophon (which releases April 9 on CD, vinyl, and digitally), is swept up in the air, too. It’s music for the planet, and a timely reminder of Earth’s fragility. People all over the world are reconnecting with nature and finding solace, rest, and peace in her arms. But The Wind also contains the sounds of Earth. Prayer flags can be heard flapping in a breeze, and piano, pipe organ, harmonium, double bass, wind chimes, and guitar are all a part of its gentle-but-stirring sound. Guitars remain light and airy, and a swooping vocal pulls the music to all four corners of the globe. The Texas-based duo of Rob Lowe and Michael A. Muller have created protective and quiet music, and the protection of the environment and the opportunity for renewal slips into the title tracks, too. ‘La Vagabonde’ is named after the catamaran that Greta Thunberg travelled on while crossing the Atlantic. Towards the end of the record’s completion, Lowe discovered a translation of the Otia Imperialia, a thirteenth-century compendium containing descriptions of marvels and miracles. Lowe was drawn to the tale of ‘The wind which St Caesarius shut up in a glove’, wherein the archbishop of Arles carries the sea breeze to a desolate valley and releases it to make the area fruitful and healthy. The same ethos can be felt in The Wind, with its life-renewing and reaffirming philosophies attaching themselves to its ambient music. www.balmorheamusic.com www.deutschegrammophon.com
items._cn_summary: Balmorhea 二人组以钢琴、管风琴、手风琴、低音提琴、风铃与吉他构建出一张关于自然与气候变迁的专辑。创作灵感横跨多重文化语境：曲名致敬 Greta Thunberg 跨大西洋航行的双体船，同时取材于十三世纪《Otia Imperialia》中圣 Caesarius 将海风引入贫瘠山谷的古老故事。专辑录音收录了经幡在风中翻动的实地声响，人声悠扬地穿梭于音景之间。整体氛围宁静而内省，音乐既是冥想式的退避，也是对地球脆弱性的温和提示。

items.body: Karine Polwart has proved herself to be an exceptional talent as a singer and songwriter for many years, all the way back to her time with Malinky (the song �Thaney� was a revelation). As a solo artist she�s grown and continually expanded her horizons, coming now to Windblown , a project that began life seven years ago, when Polwart, along with sound designer and composer Pippa Murphy, was artist in residence at Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh. The album, with its stage show and book, tells the story of the garden�s oldest specimen, a Sabal palm tree ( Sabal bermudana ), which was gently felled in 2021, and contained a surprise nobody had expected. The tree is the starting point. From there, imagination runs free. Windblown by Karine Polwart & Pippa Murphy featuring Dave Milligan It�s an album of voice and piano (the outstanding, sympathetic Dave Milligan), and, for all its global outlook on connections, one that�s very rooted in Scotland. You can hear it on the opening track, �Hear The Rigging/Last In Line,� where the melody becomes a slow, aching lament that would sound completely natural on the pipes. The stripped-down sound gives the songs both crafted stateliness and real intimacy. Each one is an exhalation, a memory, a celebration and exploration, with recurring phrases in the words and music acting as touchstones � or even hooks; they certainly stick in the mind. Windblown by Karine Polwart & Pippa Murphy featuring Dave Milligan In many ways, this is a modest album, with piano, voice and light, judicious soundscaping. It won�t overpower with noise. Yet at the same time, it�s epic, a look at history, at the flow and grandeur of nature, and the things we all carry within us. The music, and especially Polwart�s warm, compassionate voice, envelop the listener, and makes them a participant, not an observer, but a part of the journey and the history. Windblown by Karine Polwart & Pippa Murphy featuring Dave Milligan The irony arrives at the end, when the venerable old tree is down, and seeds are examined. What people for two hundred years had believed to be a Sabal bermudana turns out to be something different, a Sabal mexicana � and one of the small plants fill grow where it�s forerunner once stood. Windblown by Karine Polwart & Pippa Murphy featuring Dave Milligan Like music, plants keep to a different time � and this album/book/show give the tree the requiem it deserves, as well as hope for the future. Find the artist online. Sara Serpa - Encounters and Collisions (Review) Karine Polwart- Laws of Motion (Review) Live in the Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh, 2025

items._cn_summary: 这张作品源自苏格兰歌手Karine Polwart与声音设计师Pippa Murphy在爱丁堡皇家植物园的驻留项目，以园中最古老的一棵棕榈树为核心叙事对象。专辑以钢琴与人声为主，辅以精心设计的环境声响层，Dave Milligan的钢琴演奏克制而富有共鸣。歌曲旋律带有浓郁苏格兰民谣气质，开篇曲调如同风笛演绎的挽歌般缓慢哀婉。整体编曲追求简约与亲密感，但叙事视角从一棵树延伸至自然、历史与人类记忆的宏大图景。作品的结尾揭示了一个反讽——人们两百年间认定的树种其实是另一种棕榈树，种子将延续新生。整张专辑是为一棵古老树木谱写的安魂曲，以声音构建了一种超越时间的冥想空间，将民谣叙事、环境声音与当代作曲手法交织在一起。

items.body:
The musical partnership between Kalaniemi and Alakotila has thrived over a remarkable 35 years, long enough to the Finnish pair to develop a stunning intimacy and telepathy. Kalaniemi is a lovingly melodic accordion player, with a sharp ear for a good tune, building each one into a thing of great beauty, while pianist Alakotila not only supports her but adds enough of his own to help transform every piece into a glistening gem.
There�s a sense of calmness to the work here, a long, sweet exhalation between two instrumentalists who are deep enough in sync to allow seamless improvisation beyond any written score and carry the listeners along with them. For much of the album, it�s just the pair of them, including Kalaniemi�s wordless voice, as on the opener, the tradional �Lyck�nskan.� She does charmingly sing lyrics on the title track, written by Lasse M�rtenson, with the sound there neatly and sparingly expanded with the addition of a string quartet.
Morgondimma
There are several original pieces alongside the tradition, with Kalaniemi�s �Hambo Vid F�bodan� a real standout, and it�s perhaps inevitable on any disc featuring accordion that a Piazzolla tune should be included, brings its own shadows to the whole (�Oblivion�). And, this being Finland, a tango is almost obligatory, in this case Alakotila�s �Tango Berlin.�
Tango Berlin
There�s a gentle, dreamlike quality to so much of this, flowing and mellifluous. The pieces aren�t an arena for showy virtuosity. Instead, the two musicians serve the tune, exploring and genuinely enjoying their performances.
It won�t shake the earth, but it makes for some true listening beauty.

items._cn_summary: 这是一张芬兰手风琴与钢琴二重奏专辑，两人合作长达三十五年，默契深厚。大部分曲目仅由两人演奏，手风琴的旋律性与钢琴的和声支撑相互交织，偶尔加入弦乐四重奏或人声点缀。曲目包含传统民谣、原创作品、皮亚佐拉的探戈以及芬兰式探戈等多种风格，呈现出温柔、梦幻、流畅的质感。演奏注重旋律服务而非炫技，强调乐思的自然展开与即兴互动。整体氛围内敛而精致，适合安静聆听。作为北欧民谣与室内乐风格的结合，虽与实验、前卫等方向距离较远，但在世界音乐范畴内具有独特的地域色彩和细腻的情感表达。

items.body:
Sometime in 1986, perhaps in a Paris caf�, Dominique Cravic, a singer, guitarist, and musical archivist, met Robert Crumb, an underground cartoonist, banjo and mandolin player, and jug-band aficionado. Over a few glasses of marc, to continue to speculate, they conjured up the idea for Les Primitifs du futur.  Since then, they have recorded an impossible-to-categorize series of albums, with cover illustrations by Crumb, of which Les Crimes du Mussette is the fifth.
Weird and wonderful, it sounds like they rooted through an attic full of 78 RPM records, scribbled down some arrangements, and then played them on a collection of instruments they found in another attic, including accordion, sax, xylophone, clarinet, banjo, ukulele, theremin, Hawaiian guitar, bagpipe chanter (I�m guessing here), and musical saw.
Ne tirez pas sur le pianiste (excerpt)
The 27 short tracks are mostly voiced by Cravic, who talk-sings in the manner of an everyman Maurice Chevalier. He is often accompanied by the accordion, a customary instrument in the bal-musette style that remains a strong element of the eclectic range of styles they have managed to synthesize. They also include ragtime, jug, French chanson, and, to my ears, skiffle,  just to get the list started.
Ukulele Lady (excerpt)
The liner notes point out that �Les Crimes du Musette is also a gold mine for scholars, a veritable treasure trove.� Exploring the treasures is beyond my scope here, as each tune has a long history. A highlight for me is the humorous �Ukulele Lady� from 1925, which first delighted me on Arlo Guthrie�s 1971 album
Hobo�s Lullaby
. The song has also been covered by Bing Crosby, Peter Sellers, and Bette Midler.
N'oublie pas Gr�co (excerpt)
A more serious item is �N�oublie pas Gr�co� (Don�t Forget Gr�co�)  is a tribute to the legendary chanteuse and heroine of the French Resistance, Juliette Gr�co, who died in 2020. You will also hear old chestnuts like �Fum�e aux yeux� (�Smoke Gets in Your Eyes�),  �Boude pas� (�Take Five�), and �Prive d�amour� (�As Time Goes By�).
This record is a curiosity, but it is performed by serious musicians with total commitment. In this, I was reminded of the similarly indefinable Dan Hicks & the Hot Licks. Long-forgotten music and abandoned styles are given new animation with obvious enthusiasm and care. Speaking about himself and his collaborators, many of whom are in their seventies, Dominique Cravic says, �The young have fire, but we have light.� In its own little corner,
Les Crimes du Musette
shines bright.
Tiny Sun -
Vanishment
(Review)
Carolina Chocolate Drops -
Genuine Negro Jig
(Review)

items.body:
A debut, digital-only EP from a Danish trio, led by one of the Nordic folk scene�s outstanding and experienced vocalists, Mia Guldhammer. Five tracks, with the musicians bringing their own perspectives to mostly traditional music. There�s a lovely ancient, creaky mood throughout.
The opener, �Svennedal,� with its rough, cantering rhythm, offers a perfect shop window for Guldhammer�s impressive, persuasive voice, while jaw harp and bagpipes bring an insistent propulsion to �Nordg�rd,� the only original here, by band member Morten Musicus.
Cimbalom adds a delicate backdrop to the traditional �Agnete Of Bjergmanden,� with Guldhammer�s soft jaw harp offering extra textures to the other instruments, as it brings a springy opening to the final cut, �Orms�,� mingling with flute and strings to create something quite thrilling and off kilter on this instrumental.
Five tracks, and an introduction to a band that already seems very mature and accomplished. A strong beginning � what will GuldGanger do with an entire album?
items.label: Go' Danish Folk Music
items._cn_summary: 这是一张来自丹麦三人组合的数字EP处女作，由北欧民间音乐圈中经验丰富的歌手Mia Guldhammer领衔。五首曲目以传统素材为主，融合了口琴、风笛、扬琴、长笛与弦乐等乐器，营造出古老而略带粗粝的氛围。开篇曲以其粗犷奔放的节奏展示了主唱极具说服力的嗓音；唯一的原创曲目由乐队成员Morten Musicus创作，口琴与风笛提供了强劲的推进力。传统曲目中扬琴作为细腻背景，口琴为终曲的器乐段增添了弹性质感，与长笛和弦乐交织出不羁而扣人心弦的效果。尽管整体以传统民谣为根基，但乐器的非传统搭配与对质感的探索使作品展现出超越常规的成熟度，为听众提供了北欧民间音乐的一个独特入口。

items.body:
Live at Rockpalast 1999
documents a command performance at the Loreley open-air amphitheater by Malcolm �Mac� Rebennack Jr., aka Dr. John. Rockpalast is a live-music TV show broadcast since 1974 by Westdeutscher Rundfunk (WDR), the archival source for this CD-DVD package, and coincidentally a remarkable cultural institution on its own terms.
Taped at the height of Dr. John�s international popularity, backing the singer-pianist-guitarist are New Orleans stalwarts Bobby Broom (guitar), David Barard (bass), and Herman Ernest (drums), a tight quartet that projects authority and engages the crowd from start to close.
A striking UNESCO-designated World Heritage Site set, the Loreley is a slate pinnacle on a mythic horseshoe bend of the Rhine River, memorializing an enduring German literary legend both tragic and romantic. The setting is thus well-suited for Mac�s mystical spirit and lyrical style. By this stage of his career, he characterized his live show as a Mardi Gras revue with a mix of New Orleans standards and some of his most recognizable compositions.
Hence, he opens with the NOLA classic �Iko, Iko,� a half-sung, half-chanted celebration of community participation in the renowned Mardi Gras second-line street procession. Then comes the in-your-face boast �Qualified,� wherein the singer warns, �I got the power to control / I can see clean through you, blind mole / I want to tell you now, I'm qualified / You know that I'm qualified.�
Any Dr. John fan will recognize �I Walk on Guilded Splinters,� a moody, percussively insistent, foreboding expression of the Night Tripper�s immersion in �funknology� (his term), gris-gris herbology, and hoodoo incantation, punctuated with jungle growls and cries, a loopy, spooky slide whistle, and an extended psych-guitar solo: �Walk thru the fire / Fly thru the smoke / See my enemy / At the end of dey rope.�
Every piece in this well- honed set deserves considertion. Although Dr John lived for many years in Los Angeles and New York, his enduring hometown connection shows in the fond inclusion of his own �Sweet Home New Orleans� and �Goin� Back to New Orleans,� and he nods to a key influence with a funky rendering of Duke Ellington�s �I'm Gonna Go Fishin�.� Among other gems are Mac�s Top�10 hit �Right Place, Wrong Time,� and the instantly recognizable closer, Earl King�s �Big Chief,� another Mardi Gras burner.
Regarding his live performance approach, per the notes, �I always play a little bit of everything. I think that�s what music�s about: a little bit of somethin� old, somethin� in the middle, somethin� new, and somethin� as yet uncreated.�
Dr John's�s longtime fans will welcome this archival gem, which also is a solid introduction for any late comers to the party. Surmounting the barriers of language and culture, the power of
At the Rockpalast
is also evident in the enthusiastic audience response. As he declares, �If you�re gonna get off on somethin� you don�t need to know nothin� about it. Music is a universal language.�

items.body: Review by Fercandio46 — As long as the Electric Light Orchestra maintained the premise of being a progressive rock band featuring strings, they could rely on those very strings, along with the right arrangements, to remain at the cutting edge. However, with each successive album following Roy Wood's departure, pop music began to take up more space in their compositions. "Fire on High" boasts a sweeping, powerful start, moving beyond the intro and the female chorus to showcase that signature element established in their first three albums: a classical-rock orchestra. Yet, while the compositions on those early records were daring and surprising, featuring dark, original arrangements that coexisted with rock 'n' roll, the music gradually became more predictable. Face the Music is an enjoyable listen, though it has its ups and downs; "Waterfall," for instance, is a ballad that, were the strings stripped away, I could easily imagine Freddie Mercury singing. Those strings could be mysterious, aggressive, or melancholic, and at times even reminiscent of the Beatles, echoing the production style of George Martin."Evil Woman" is a great song, the first of the nods to disco they would incorporate, yet played in a glam-rock and funk style. It's a spirited, groovy track featuring prominent drums and Bee Gees-style backing vocals; the strings serve the disco vibe, complemented by a funky clavinet part that made, and still makes, the song a lot of fun (proving that progressive rock can be fun, too). At times, the strings would play around and break the conventional mold, and whenever Jeff Lynne was in a festive mood, he really brought a great vibe to the music."Nightrider" is built upon the backing vocals and all the signature trappings they had established, the voices and the swirling strings that seemed to spin like a Ferris wheel. Yet, it still sounded fresh; at times, the music would hang suspended in mid-air, leaving the female backing vocals alone for a few seconds before everything instantly rushed back in. There was also a dreamlike section, a compositional triumph, infused with a burst of energy that snapped the listener out of that reverie; it was in moments like these that ELO truly shone with a symphonic brilliance."Poker" was another fast-paced rock 'n' roll track, yet Richard Tandy's Minimoog, Lynne's guitar, and the cellos combined to create magnificent sonic moments; meanwhile, "Strange Magic", which begins like Tchaikovsky's Swan Lake, transforms into a radio-friendly mid-70s ballad. For some reason, the influence of the Bee Gees and Queen hovers over the album, intertwining with the electric originality of this orchestra. "Down Home Town" succumbs to an inexplicable country vibe, though the string arrangements are effectively tailored to that style. "One Summer Dream" begins with the gravity of an opera's finale, with melancholy taking the lead, yet it balances out a solid, worthy album that delivers all the virtues and strengths one would expect from the band. The choruses and those robust string parts the band could latch onto saved it from the electric chair, which they could simply walk right past.

items._cn_summary: 这张1975年的专辑延续了将弦乐融入摇滚的编制思路，但整体趋势明显从早期大胆原创的暗黑交响编排向更可预测的流行化方向倾斜。开篇以恢宏弦乐与古典摇滚管弦乐质感切入，随后各曲风走向各异：Disco元素与放克Clavinet注入舞曲律动，贝斯吉斯式和声铺陈助兴；某些段落以旋转式弦乐织体悬置空中，配合女声和声与梦境段落展现出真正交响辉煌时刻；快速摇滚曲中Minimoog、电吉他与大提琴交织出辉煌声响瞬间。然而部分曲目过度依赖弦乐伪装以掩盖本质上的七十年代中期抒情流行与乡村质感，创作上趋于保守、惊喜减少。作为向商业化过渡的转折点，编曲精致但创新性有限，更接近主流摇滚受众而非前卫实验领域。

items.body: Belgian electronica pop act 808 Dot Pop has posted four videos since 14 August 2026, each pairing a track from an ongoing “-ism” naming series with a 20th-century building, ahead of two albums, “Minimalism” and “Maximalism,” due at the end of November 2026 via Alfa Matrix. The most recent, “Collectionism,” was posted on the artist’s official website on 17 September 2026. The four videos “Internationalism (Seagram)” was posted around 28 August 2026 and pairs the track with the Seagram Building in New York, an example of the International Style. The track itself is not available on the video’s own release: it appears exclusively on the various-artists compilation “Sounds From The Matrix 26” and will not be issued elsewhere. “Brutalism (Habitat 67)” followed on 6 September 2026, built around Moshe Safdie’s Habitat 67 in Montreal. The visual is as a digital reinterpretation of the building via “The Hillside Project” by NeoScape, rather than footage of the original structure. “Contextualism (Fallingwater)” was posted on 11 September 2026, pairing the track with Frank Lloyd Wright’s Fallingwater house. The version of “Contextualism” heard in this video appears on the “Minimalism” album, while a separate version of the same track, tied to the AT&T Long Lines Building, features on the lead single “Minimalism,” due 26 September 2026. “Collectionism” was posted on 17 September 2026. Unlike the previous three entries in this video 808 Dot Pop gives more info on a few upcoming fan packages. The ‘Minimalism’ and ‘Maximalism’ project 808 Dot Pop announced “Minimalism” (a white-sleeve album) and “Maximalism” (a black-sleeve album) on its website on 14 August 2026, describing them as “two completely different albums in content.” The lead single, “Minimalism,” is scheduled for 26 September 2026. Two further items are tied to the same releases. “Foundationalism,” a six-track EP featuring exclusive versions, is planned as a fan-shop exclusive on an NFC-equipped “phygital” card format. A 72-page fan book titled “Essentialism,” covering the architectural sites referenced across the campaign, was announced on 11 September 2026, with further details promised but not yet published as of this writing. A full tracklist and confirmed formats for “Minimalism” and “Maximalism” have not been published. About 808 Dot Pop 808 Dot Pop is the solo electronica pop project of Belgian musician Passenger S, also known for his work in Metroland. Side-Line reported his debut under the 808 Dot Pop name on 27 March 2020, in “Metroland’s Passenger S launches debut album under 808 DOT POP moniker”, ahead of the album “The Colour Temperature,” released on download and CD on 5 June 2020 on Alfa Matrix. Further singles followed the same year: “Incandescent,” the second single from “The Colour Temperature,” on 19 June 2020; a tribute cover of D.A.F.’s “El Que” for Alfa Matrix’s “Wir Sind DAF” compilation, released 2 October 2020; and “Kelvin (4200),” the third and final single from the debut album, on 13 November 2020, alongside a bundled triple 7-inch vinyl set covered by Side-Line in “Electro pop act 808 Dot Pop releases triple 7 inch vinyl singles in one bundle + 2 new download only singles” (6 November 2020). Side-Line also ran a ‘Click Interview’ with 808 Dot Pop in July 2020. The project continued with the “Ultraviolet” single campaign (February 2021) ahead of the album “The Cubic Temperature,” the “SunCatcher” EP (early March 2022) and a single dedicated to Guglielmo Marconi (January 2023), the latter featuring lyrics by Gary Hunter (Kraftman) and vocals by Lis Van Den Akker. Side-Line covered the act’s return with three simultaneous albums plus two EPs in “Belgian electronica act 808 Dot Pop back with 3 albums in one go + 2 singles” (27 March 2023) and a further double-EP release in “Electronica pop act 808 DOT POP returns with double EP” (5 June 2023). Most recently, fellow Alfa Matrix artist Cubic issued a rework album built on 808 Dot Pop material, covered by Side-Line in “Cubic drops 808 Dot Pop rework album ‘Back To 808’ on Alfa Matrix” (12 December 2025). The four-video architecture series and the wider “Minimalism”/”Maximalism” campaign mark the act’s first new album cycle since 2023.
items._cn_summary: 比利时电子流行艺人808 Dot Pop（Passenger S的另一个项目）以一系列以"主义"命名的歌曲搭配二十世纪标志性建筑的视频预告了两张风格对立的双专辑《Minimalism》与《Maximalism》，计划于2026年底通过Alfa Matrix厂牌发行。从已发布的四支视频来看，作品以建筑为视觉主题，将Internationalism、Brutalism、Contextualism等概念分别与Seagram大厦、Habitat 67、Fallingwater等建筑对应，曲名贯穿哲学与建筑批评的词汇。其中部分曲目仅收录于合辑或实体限量载体（如NFC"phygital"卡片和72页粉丝书），体现出对发行形式的实验性思考。整体概念偏重于视觉与文本层面的建筑隐喻，但文章作为新闻稿性质的信息通告，对音乐本身的声响特质、制作手法和艺术成几乎没有涉及，无法对实际听感做出判断。

items.album: Ray Noir releases ‘Gothstar’ EP with Danny Blu collaboration and new track ‘Crush’
items.excerpt: London-based queer alt-metal artist Ray Noir released “Gothstar” on September 17th 2026, a six-track EP that mixes metalcore guitars with rave and electronic club production. Ray Noir’s “Gothstar” EP is out digitally and on vinyl and CD. The EP collects the four singles issued since April 2026 and adds two new recordings. It opens with “Label Whxre” and continues with “Black”, “Boys”, and “Gothstar” featuring Danny Blu
items.body: London-based queer alt-metal artist Ray Noir released “Gothstar” on September 17th 2026, a six-track EP that mixes metalcore guitars with rave and electronic club production. Ray Noir’s “Gothstar” EP is out digitally and on vinyl and CD. The EP collects the four singles issued since April 2026 and adds two new recordings. It opens with “Label Whxre” and continues with “Black”, “Boys”, and “Gothstar” featuring Danny Blu, the New York artist and former Echo Black frontman. The new track “Crush” follows, and “Gothstar (Alternative Version)”, a solo version of the title track, closes the record. Ray Noir wrote the material with Jon Cass and Tom Saint, who are also the EP’s producers. The track credits for “Black” and “Crush” list Cass as producer and Saint for additional production, mixing and mastering, with Saint also singing backing vocals on “Crush”. Cass, a member of UK post-hardcore band As Everything Unfolds, previously produced Ray Noir’s 2025 EP “Against The Machine”. The release material describes the EP as dealing with identity, confidence and sexuality, with “Gothstar” as both a character and an attitude at its centre. Ray Noir commented: “Growing up in the Norwegian metal scene, I didn’t really see anyone like me. With Gothstar, I wanted to create the world I wish I’d had back then. It’s gay, it’s heavy, it’s sweaty, it’s camp and it doesn’t take itself too seriously. Basically, if Berghain had a mosh pit, I’d like to think this would be playing.” “Crush” is the focus track of the EP. Ray Noir based it on his own experience of growing up in Norway’s metal scene and on “Heated Rivalry”, Rachel Reid’s gay ice hockey romance novel, which was adapted for television in 2025. The lyrics name the story’s lead couple, Ilya and Shane, and include lines in Norwegian. Four singles ahead of the EP “Label Whxre” opened the “Gothstar” campaign on 2 April 2026. “Black” followed on 14 May 2026 with a video directed by Ray Noir, and “Boys” arrived in June 2026 with a video filmed at Slim Jim’s Liquor Store in Islington, north London. The title track “Gothstar” featuring Danny Blu came out on 13 August 2026 together with an official music video. ‘Gothstar'”‘ release party in London Ray Noir marks the release with a party at Slim Jim’s Liquor Store on Saturday 19 September 2026, the venue where the “Boys” video was filmed. Tom Saint is listed as special guest. Entry is free, with tickets via Ray Noir – Gothstar EP Release Party on DICE. Get the EP as vinyl or CD here! About Ray Noir Ray Noir is a queer alternative artist based in London. His official biography places his background in Oslo’s black-metal underground, and his sound combines metal guitars with electronic club production. He released his first single, “Double Trouble”, in 2014. In October 2023 he issued “Pity Party“, the lead single from the mixtape “Scorpio”, followed on 1 November 2023 by “Latency“. The seven-track “Scorpio” arrived in 2024, and his official biography lists a top-five placement in the German Alternative Charts. A deluxe edition of “Scorpio” followed in July 2024, adding “All Alone” featuring Mariann Rosa of Surferosa, a “Double Trouble” remix by TOVA, remixes by Gothminister, Corlyx and Tension Control, and “You, Me & The Devil” featuring Tom Saint. That August he supported Combichrist at the Underworld in London and played the Electro Night in Oslo at Revolver with Piston Damp on 31 August 2024. On 14 February 2025 he released “Razorblade Romance“, written with Steve Stevens and Madeleine Wood, featuring Stevens on guitar and produced and mixed by Jon Cass. A cover of Tears for Fears’ “Shout” followed in May 2025, with guitar by Arno Von Detritus and backing vocals by Ben Christo of The Sisters of Mercy. “Dead Valentine” came out on 3 July 2025 and announced the EP “Against The Machine”, released on 18 September 2025 with “Razorblade Romance”, “Dead Valentine”, “Mad World” and an alternative version of “YMATD”. A deluxe edition followed in December 2025 with remixes by Tension Control, Verona On Venus, Junkie Kut and Ays Kura, alongside vinyl and CD editions. Ray Noir opened 2026 with the singles “Temptation” in January and “Breathe” in February. “Gothstar” is his second EP after “Against The Machine” and continues his work with Jon Cass, who produced both EPs, and Tom Saint, who also featured on the 2024 “Scorpio” deluxe edition.
items._cn_summary: Ray Noir的《Gothstar》EP将金属核吉他与锐舞电子舞曲制作相融合，六首曲目围绕身份认同、性别自信与酷儿议题展开。制作方面由Jon Cass与Tom Saint操刀，部分单曲配有影像版本。作品概念以"Gothstar"为核心角色与态度，试图构建一个融合哥特、重型与俱乐部文化的虚构世界。引文中提到Berghain与mosh pit的意象，暗示创作者试图在重型音乐场景中注入夜店美学。虽然融合了金属与电子，但整体仍属另类金属框架内的常规操作，缺乏深度的声音实验或结构性突破，主题表达也偏向流行化的酷儿宣言而非音乐语言的革新。作为一篇资讯性新闻稿，提供了发行信息和创作背景，但缺少对音乐本身的深度评析。

items.body: Boston publisher SIGNALS Press launched a Kickstarter campaign on 10 September 2026 for “Industrial Music/Graphics: A Visual History of a Movement“, a 320-page survey of the graphic design that grew up alongside industrial music. The campaign runs through 2 October 2026, with books shipping spring 2027. The book traces the movement’s visual language from post-punk Britain and Cold War Europe through Reagan-era America, across album covers, logos, posters, type studies and ephemera. It documents the graphic identities of bands and labels including Throbbing Gristle and Industrial Records, Cabaret Voltaire, Mute Records, Nettwerk, wax trax!, Einstürzende Neubauten, Skinny Puppy, Front 242, Ministry, KMFDM and Nine Inch Nails. Designers contributing directly to the book include Neville Brody, Rob Sheridan, Richard Borge, Rick Valicenti, Patrick Codenys, Steven R. Gilmore, Simon Granger, Simone Grant, Brian Shanley and Martin Atkins. The Kickstarter’s reward tiers include a pin designed by Simon Granger of Nitzer Ebb Produkt and two shirts by Steven R. Gilmore. “Industrial music didn’t just change how music sounded, it changed how music looked,” said coauthor Chris Grimley. “Designers were sampling medical imagery, military documents, brutalist architecture, and early computer graphics into something coherent and international, and that history has never been collected. It sits in aftermarket bins and collectors’ stacks. This book brings it together.” The book is authored by GR—APP, the shared pseudonym of Chris Grimley and Alan Rapp. Grimley is founder and creative director of SIGNALS Press and has authored, coauthored and designed numerous books; Rapp is editorial director of SIGNALS Press and a former college DJ and music critic. “Industrial Music/Graphics” is produced as a physical object in its own right: 8 x 10.25 inches, 320 pages, Otabind layflat binding, four-color interior and a six-color foil-stamped, offset-printed cover. The Kickstarter campaign carries a Kickstarter “Project We Love” designation. About SIGNALS Press SIGNALS Press is a Boston-based publisher founded and led by Chris Grimley, who has authored, coauthored and designed multiple books and began making music after covering Skinny Puppy in high school. Alan Rapp, the press’s editorial director, is a former college DJ and music critic. Together the pair write as GR—APP, a pseudonym paying homage to the artistic aliases adopted by figures within the industrial scene the book documents. “Industrial Music/Graphics: A Visual History of a Movement” is SIGNALS Press’s Kickstarter campaign running through 2 October 2026, with fulfillment planned for spring 2027.
items._cn_summary: 本文为Side-Line刊载的Kickstarter众筹新闻稿，介绍波士顿出版社SIGNALS Press推出的工业音乐平面设计图鉴。该书为320页视觉史著作，系统梳理工业音乐运动中的唱片封面、标识、海报等视觉语汇，从后朋克英国与冷战欧洲延伸至里根时期美国，记录Throbbing Gristle、Cabaret Voltaire、Nitzer Ebb、Skinny Puppy、Front 242、Nine Inch Nails等乐队及厂牌的视觉设计脉络。Neville Brody、Rob Sheridan等设计师直接参与内容贡献。书籍采用Otabind平摊装订、四色内页与六色烫金封面制作，并获Kickstarter"Project We Love"认证。本文并非音乐评论，而是出版众筹公告，与用户关注的实验、爵士、电子融合等听觉领域内容相关性有限。

items.body: UK synthpop and dark disco project KN/GHTS released the single “Light The Fuse” on 17 September 2026 via Specchio Uomo. The B-side carries a remix of “Supernatural Lover”, from KN/GHTS’s second studio album of the same name, by Berlin-based artist Daniel Knutz. Light The Fuse by KN/GHTS Specchio Uomo describes “Light The Fuse” as a pulsating and emotionally charged song about loss, recovery and finding yourself again. The track mixes synth pop, dark disco and italo disco elements with classic synth sounds. Daniel Knutz, whose own work draws on darkwave, coldwave, post-punk and minimal electronic, reworks “Supernatural Lover” as the release’s second track. An official video for “Light The Fuse” is out now, directed and edited by independent filmmaker Dirk Roche. It was filmed during the “Supernatural Lover Tour”, with additional footage from KN/GHTS’s live performances in Germany. About KN/GHTS KN/GHTS is the solo project of UK vocalist and songwriter James Knights, previously a singer of electronic pioneers Boytronic and known from his time in Scarlet Soho. Knights launched the project under the name Knight$, releasing the EPs “What’s Your Poison?” (2016) and “Alligator” (2017) before his debut album “Dollar$ & Cent$” came out on Cargo Records in 2019. Side-Line spoke to him about that album in a 2019 interview, in which he described the project as a faster-moving continuation of the sound he built with Scarlet Soho and Boytronic. The project later restyled its name as KN/GHTS and released its second studio album, “Supernatural Lover”, building an audience particularly in Germany, Sweden and Mexico. KN/GHTS combines synth pop, dark disco, electronic music and theatrical performance, and has performed live alongside Drab Majesty and Andy Bell of Erasure. “Light The Fuse”, released via Specchio Uomo, continues the project’s work following the “Supernatural Lover” album and tour.

items.body: Charlotte, North Carolina synthpop project Midniter, the solo vehicle of Nic Pugh, released the single and video “I Could Love You” on September 15, 2026, via Bandcamp and YouTube. It is the fourth and final promotional single ahead of Midniter’s debut album, “Xeno”, due October 27 on SugarTank! Records, the Charlotte label Pugh co-founded. The release coincides with the opening of vinyl LP pre-orders for “Xeno” through the label’s own store. Midniter describes “I Could Love You” as a ballad about unrequited love Pugh traced the song back to an unfinished piano piece: “‘I Could Love You’ came from an old piano tune that I never finished. The bookends of the song are directly from that idea, with the middle evolving into a more synthpop direction for Midniter. To me, it’s a pretty standard ballad about unrequited love – a tale as old as time that everyone can understand.” I Could Love You by Midniter The video for “I Could Love You” favors mood over narrative Pugh said the video leaves its meaning open: “The video is more ambiguous, playing with the question, ‘Is this about desire, obsession, or both?’ It’s ultimately your call to make. Our goal with this video was to focus more on mood than narrative. It was more important to live in these feelings of distance and longing than explain why they linger. The dancers, our friends from Baran Dance, were instrumental in carrying those moods throughout the video with their choreography. Our main actress Dustie Bayer was also incredible in her debut.” Paul Jahn of Yawn Productions filmed and edited the video, co-directing it with Pugh. Choreography comes from Baran Dance members Audrey Baran, Faith Centa and Donovan Granville, with Dustie Bayer in the lead acting role. For the silhouette performance scenes, Midniter expands to a trio with Joe Boyland and Dan Hitzelberger joining Pugh. Filming took place at Petra’s, the Charlotte venue where Pugh works and where Midniter’s 2025 debut single video, “Shoot the Moon”, was also shot, alongside a University of North Carolina dance studio and locations around Charlotte. About Midniter Midniter is the solo indie-electronic project of Charlotte, North Carolina musician Nic Pugh, launched in 2024 after roughly two decades in punk and rock’n’roll bands, including Paint Fumes and Jaggermouth. As Midniter, Pugh mixes synthpop songwriting with indie-electronic production, citing Radiohead, Justice, The Knife, LCD Soundsystem, Aphex Twin, Squarepusher and M83 as reference points alongside an “Indie Sleaze” visual style. Pugh co-founded Charlotte label SugarTank! Records with fellow musician Nic Holman; the label supports LGBTQ+ artists and allies. Midniter’s debut single, “Shoot the Moon”, arrived with a video shot at Petra’s in 2025, and Side-Line covered the project’s “Alarmist” video single that October. “I Could Love You” is the fourth and last of the promotional singles released ahead of Midniter’s debut album, “Xeno”, due October 27 on SugarTank! Records, with vinyl LP pre-orders now open through the label.

items.body: Cocteau Twins released their sixth studio album, “Heaven or Las Vegas,” through 4AD on 17 September 1990, with Capitol Records distributing the album in the United States. The dream pop record turns 36 this year. The trio, vocalist Elizabeth Fraser, guitarist Robin Guthrie and bassist Simon Raymonde, wrote, recorded and produced “Heaven or Las Vegas” themselves at September Sound, the studio Guthrie set up inside Pete Townshend’s former Eel Pie Studios in Twickenham. The ten-track album opens with “Cherry-coloured Funk” and “Pitch the Baby” and also includes “Iceblink Luck,” “Fifty-fifty Clown,” the title track “Heaven or Las Vegas,” “I Wear Your Ring,” “Fotzepolitic,” “Wolf in the Breast,” “Road, River and Rail” and closer “Frou-frou Foxes in Midsummer Fires.” It followed 1988’s “Blue Bell Knoll” and reached number seven on the UK Albums Chart and number 99 on the US Billboard 200. “Heaven or Las Vegas” streams on Spotify. About Cocteau Twins Cocteau Twins formed in 1979 in Grangemouth, Scotland, when guitarist Robin Guthrie and bassist Will Heggie began writing songs together, taking their name from a song by fellow Scottish band Simple Minds. Guthrie met 17-year-old Elizabeth Fraser at a Falkirk disco in 1981 and invited her to sing; her wordless, high-register vocal style became the group’s signature. The trio signed to 4AD in 1982 and released their debut album, “Garlands,” the same year, followed by “Head over Heels” in 1983. Heggie left after “Head over Heels” and was replaced by multi-instrumentalist Simon Raymonde, who joined in time for 1984’s “Treasure,” the band’s first UK Top 40 album. Cocteau Twins released two albums in 1986, “Victorialand” and a collaboration with ambient composer Harold Budd titled “The Moon and the Melodies,” before “Blue Bell Knoll” (1988) became their first record to chart on the US Billboard 200. “Heaven or Las Vegas” followed on 17 September 1990, recorded and self-produced at the band’s own September Sound studio, and became the trio’s highest-charting UK album. Cocteau Twins left 4AD after the record and signed to Fontana, releasing “Four-Calendar Café” (1993) and “Milk & Kisses” (1996) before disbanding in 1997. Guthrie and Raymonde have continued releasing music individually since: Side-Line reported on Raymonde’s Bella Union label presenting the debut album by his project Lost Horizons in 2017, and on Guthrie’s ‘Riviera’ EP in 2021 and his 60th-birthday ‘Springtime’ EP in 2022. Fraser also returned to recording in 2022, her first new material in 13 years, as Side-Line reported. “Heaven or Las Vegas” turns 36 this year, still marking the commercial high point of the band’s decade-long run on 4AD.
items._cn_summary: 这是一篇关于Cocteau Twins第六张专辑《Heaven or Las Vegas》发行36周年的纪念性新闻稿，主要介绍了专辑的发行信息、录制背景及乐队历史。文章以平铺直叙的方式列出了曲目列表、厂牌4AD与Capitol的发行关系、录音室九月之声（位于Twickenham的Pete Townshend前Eel Pie Studios）的位置，以及该专辑在英国专辑榜第七、美国公告牌200第九十九的榜单成绩。同时概述了乐队从1979年成立至1997年解散的历程，以及成员后续的个人音乐动向。作为dream pop与ethereal wave的代表，Cocteau Twins以Elizabeth Fraser无歌词的高音人声和Robin Guthrie层层叠叠的吉他音墙著称，但本文偏向事实陈述而非音乐分析，缺乏对声音设计、制作手法或艺术创新的深入探讨。

items.body: Mute have shared the newly remastered Coil track “Either His, or Yours”, the third track revealed from “Gold is the Metal (With the Broadest Shoulders),” due on limited-edition vinyl, CD and digitally on 30 October 2026 through Mute and Coil’s own imprint Threshold House. Side-Line covered the reissue’s announcement and its first single, “Cardinal Points,” in July, when Mute and Threshold House confirmed the 30 October release date and the reissue’s catalog number, COIL3. “Either His, or Yours” follows that track and the subsequent “Aqua Regalia” as the reissue’s third pre-release song, and sits at position thirteen on the album’s sixteen-track sequence. “Gold is the Metal (With the Broadest Shoulders)” is the closing album in a trilogy that began with “Scatology” (1984) and “Horse Rotorvator” (1986), drawing on textural and instrumental material sidelined during “Horse Rotorvator’s” sequencing. The reissue restores artwork reconstructed by Stephen Thrower and his partner Ossian Brown (a member of Coil from 1999 to 2004), using archive material that includes artefacts, photographs and personal notes made by the late John Balance, alongside new sleeve notes. It is the first release in a new partnership between Mute and Threshold House that will bring four early Coil albums back into print with restored artwork and previously unseen imagery. Coil’s “Gold is the Metal” release details The album’s full, sixteen-track running order remains “The Last Rites of Spring,” “Paradisiac,” “Thump,” “For Us They Will,” “The Broken Wheel,” “Boy in a Suitcase,” “Golden Hole,” “Cardinal Points,” “Red Slur,” “…Of Free Enterprise,” “Aqua Regalia,” “Metal in the Head,” “Either His, or Yours,” “Chickenskin,” “Soundtrap” and “The First Five Minutes after Violent Death,” all carrying the 2026 remaster. Mute and Threshold House plan to follow “Gold is the Metal” with further early Coil reissues: the soundtrack for Derek Jarman’s “The Angelic Conversation,” the previously unreleased music Coil recorded for Clive Barker’s “Hellraiser,” and the compilation “Unnatural History.” About Coil Coil formed in London in 1982 as a solo project of John Balance (born Geoffrey Burton, 1962-2004), then a member of Psychic TV. The project became a duo when Balance’s partner Peter Christopherson (1955-2010), formerly of Throbbing Gristle, joined him. Coil’s first release, the one-sided 12″ single “How to Destroy Angels,” came out in 1984. Stephen Thrower joined the group during the recording of “Horse Rotorvator” (1986) and remained through “Gold is the Metal (With the Broadest Shoulders)” (1987), the third and closing album of a trilogy that also included “Scatology” (1984). Coil released music through the 1990s and 2000s that ranged from the industrial dance of “Windowpane” to the ambient “Time Machines” (1998) and the two-volume “Musick to Play in the Dark.” John Balance died in 2004 after a fall at the band’s home, and Coil effectively ended; Peter Christopherson continued to oversee reissues of the group’s catalog until his own death in 2010. In July 2026, Mute and Threshold House announced the “Gold is the Metal (With the Broadest Shoulders)” reissue for 30 October, along with its first single, “Cardinal Points,” followed by a second track, “Aqua Regalia.” “Either His, or Yours” is the third song to surface ahead of that release date.
items._cn_summary: 本文为Mute厂牌与Threshold House合作重新发行Coil乐队专辑《Gold is the Metal (With the Broadest Shoulders)》的资讯稿。专辑原为1980年代后期录制，作为继《Scatology》（1984）和《Horse Rotorvator》（1986）之后的收官之作，素材源自《Horse Rotorvator》制作期间被搁置的器乐与质感化片段。2026年新版经过重新母带处理，由Stephen Thrower与Ossian Brown利用John Balance遗留的档案、照片及手稿重建封面与内页设计。文章详细列出了十六首曲目的完整顺序，并预告了后续将再版《The Angelic Conversation》电影原声、Coil为Clive Barker《Hellraiser》录制的未发行配乐，以及选辑《Unnatural History》。但内容本身更偏向发行公告与曲目罗列，缺乏对音乐本体、制作方式或艺术价值的深度评述。

items.body: Los Angeles club Das Bunker marks its 30th anniversary this October with three events: a Catch One show headlined by Combichrist on October 2, a Nine Inch Nails-themed boat cruise called Nine Inch Sails on October 10, and a Halloween dance party on October 31. Combichrist headlines Das Bunker’s 30th anniversary at Catch One Combichrist returns to Das Bunker for the first time since 2009 to headline the club’s official 30th anniversary show at Catch One on October 2. The set draws on the band’s first three albums, “The Joy of Gunz” (2003), “Everybody Hates You” (2005) and “What The Fuck Is Wrong With You People?” (2007). Richmond, Virginia’s The Treasury, whose sound mixes EBM, synth-punk, post-punk and 1990s techno, opens. Das Bunker resident DJs Mimi Cry, IHX, Franck H Bomb and The Operative play the rest of the 21+ night, which runs from 9pm to 3am. A Nine Inch Nails boat cruise and a Halloween party close out the month On October 10, Nine Inch Sails departs from Long Beach, California, the port city where Das Bunker started as a club. Das Bunker offshoot 90s Goth Klub and Depeche Boat present the 21+, three-hour, two-room cruise: DJ Bractune plays Nine Inch Nails on the outdoor deck while DJ Eser covers goth, darkwave and new wave on the second room. The anniversary month closes on October 31 with a Halloween party at Catch One, presented by 90s Goth Klub and Body Rhythm across two rooms of goth, darkwave and new wave. DJs J Bractune, Rev.John and Angel Tears play the 21+ event. About Das Bunker Das Bunker was founded in Long Beach, California on October 22, 1996, to spotlight industrial and related genres that other Los Angeles clubs overlooked before relocating its regular night to Catch One. Over three decades the club has hosted Front 242 and other established industrial and EBM acts alongside emerging names, and has run recurring nights including History of Industrial, Summer Massive and Das Bunker Star Wars Night. Its coverage has included the Los Angeles Times, Vice and Post Punk. Side-Line covered Das Bunker’s 29th anniversary last October, when Unter Null headlined at Catch One. This year’s 30th anniversary run adds Combichrist, a Nine Inch Nails cruise and a Halloween party to that annual tradition.
items._cn_summary: 本文为Side-Line发布的纯新闻稿，报道洛杉矶地下俱乐部Das Bunker成立30周年的三场庆祝活动。第一场由工业/EBM乐队Combichrist领衔，曲目涵盖其前三张专辑；第二场为Nine Inch Nails主题游船派对，由DJ分别播放NIN曲目和哥特/暗潮/新浪潮；第三场为万圣节舞会，同样以哥特、暗潮和新浪潮为主打。文章介绍了Das Bunker的历史背景——1996年在长滩创立，专注于工业及周边流派的推广，曾承办Front 242等知名乐队的演出。整体内容属于活动资讯而非乐评，未涉及音乐本身的艺术分析或声音评价，对暗潮/工业/电子领域关注者有一定信息参考价值。

items.body: Aggrotech and dark electro project Subliminal Code released an official video for “Behind the Mask“, the title track from the single issued through Neon Retro Records on July 31, 2026. Side-Line covered the single’s five-track remix package when a People Theatre remix, an Elektroterapi remix, a club version and a Dominator remix were added on August 16; the video now gives the title track its own visual counterpart. The project describes its sound as combining “Industrial, Aggrotech, Dark Electro, EBM and Hard Techno”, and says “Behind the Mask” continues that direction with “a cinematic visual concept inspired by classic psychological horror and 80s slasher cinema.” Behind the Mask by Subliminal Code About Subliminal Code Subliminal Code was founded at the start of 2010 by Raul Jose Padron and Raul Junior Padron, drawing on EBM, industrial, metal and synthpop; the twin brothers trace their roots to Venezuela, with the project now based between Venezuela and Hungary. Side-Line has followed the project’s chronology from the “Malevolencia” single in 2020 through the “The Cancer Of The World Is Human Beings” album in 2021 and on to the “Behind the Mask” single and its remix package this year. “Behind the Mask” is the first Subliminal Code release to carry Neon Retro Records, and the new video is its first official visual.
